edits.anchor: · A syndrome that carries Wilms risk earns surveillance ultrasounds
edits.html: · Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome raises the risk of both Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma, so the syndrome alone cannot pick between them · A firm right upper quadrant mass with a very high AFP (alpha-fetoprotein) in an infant is hepatoblastoma · How NBME framed it: the stem names the syndrome and hides the answer in a lab panel, a very high AFP with normal urine HVA (homovanillic acid) and VMA (vanillylmandelic acid)
edits.note: NBME Q22 deciding finding and framing

edits.anchor: Renal cell carcinoma arises within the kidney too, but in adults.
edits.html:
Salient decoyWilms tumor (nephroblastoma) — the best-known Beckwith-Wiedemann tumor, but it is a flank mass within the kidney and does not raise AFP (alpha-fetoprotein).
Test-overrides-findingsNeuroblastoma — age 6 months fits it better than Wilms tumor, but urine HVA (homovanillic acid) and VMA (vanillylmandelic acid) are normal.
Unchecked attributeGerm cell tumor — a yolk sac tumor also raises AFP, but in a young child it presents as a pelvic mass, not a firm upper abdominal one.
True-fact-wrong-slotSpina bifida occulta — a raised AFP goes with open neural tube defects in pregnancy, not the closed form, and it makes no abdominal mass.
